# Buffer incoming Wants until the Dart consumer is ready

## Platform difference

Native launch events can arrive before the Flutter engine and Dart subscriptions are ready.

## Implementation

LocalSend uses warm-launch EventChannel delivery and a cold-launch URI mailbox consumed during preInit. A follow-up clears stale mailboxes, decodes filenames and moves copy work into initialization. Pica Comic similarly retains incoming widget/continuation actions until application handlers are ready rather than injecting a route too early.

## Applicability

Applies to share targets, native cards and other external entrypoints. Keep an explicit ownership/consumption rule for pending payloads.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

LocalSend still does not explicitly await its asynchronous shared-data request before engine startup in the inspected change, so the mailbox is not proof of a race-free implementation. Avoid duplicate delivery and stale replay after unrelated launches.

## Verification

Test cold process start, already-running app, delayed engine initialization, repeated Wants, malformed URIs and process death between persistence and consumption.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.

updates.notes: Android follow-ups isolate malformed notification activation from ordinary launch, validate schedule data, surface failures and retain a bounded diagnostic record when consumed fires fail at startCore, background submission or delivery. Later changes keep retention under schedule lock, log cap drops and separate retentionError from the original failure. Handoff submission is not delivery; retained failure is diagnostic, not durable automatic retry/replay. Extended existing lifecycle ingress lesson at protocol/ownership boundary. No new OH Want/scheduler backend or runtime behavior established; OH requires its own delivery and persistence acceptance tests.
